# omada_controller_settings (Resource)

Manages controller-wide settings (Global Settings → Controller Settings).

~> **This resource is controller-scoped and has no `site`.** It is a singleton: there is one such document per controller, so declare at most one of these.

~> **`device_host` is the setting most worth managing here.** It is the address adopted devices are told to contact. Left to the controller, it is inferred from the host's interfaces and can land on one nothing can reach — a VPN tunnel, say — after which devices drop off some time later and look like flaky hardware rather than a misconfiguration.

Every attribute is optional and only what you set is sent. Anything you leave out keeps its current value and will never report drift. `terraform destroy` forgets the settings without changing the controller.

SMTP, certificates and the RADIUS blocks are deliberately not managed here: they carry credentials and key material that belong in their own resources.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Controller-wide settings. This resource is controller-scoped: unlike every
# other resource in this provider it takes no `site`, and there is exactly one
# of it per controller.
resource "omada_controller_settings" "this" {
  name      = "home"
  time_zone = "America/Los_Angeles"
  region    = "United States"

  # The address adopted devices are told to phone home to.
  #
  # Worth setting explicitly. Left alone, the controller infers one from its
  # host's interfaces, and on a host with a VPN tunnel or several NICs it can
  # pick one the devices cannot reach. Devices then drop off some time later
  # and the symptom looks like flaky hardware.
  device_host_enable = true
  device_host        = "omada.example.com"

  # The address the controller uses for its own links and portal URLs.
  host_name = "omada.example.com"

  # An adopted device's own web UI takes a password, so do not offer it
  # over plain HTTP.
  device_web_control_http  = false
  device_web_control_https = true
}

# Anything you leave out keeps whatever the controller already has and never
# reports drift, so managing two fields is a perfectly good use of this
# resource:
#
#   resource "omada_controller_settings" "this" {
#     device_host_enable = true
#     device_host        = "10.0.0.10"
#   }
#
# Declare only one of these, though. Two would each read the document, write
# their own sections, and fight over anything they both set.
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Optional

- `app_discovery` (Boolean) Answer discovery probes from the Omada mobile app on the local network.
- `device_host` (String) The address adopted devices are told to contact.

~> Must be reachable **from the devices**, which is not always the address you reach the controller on. A controller on a host with several interfaces will otherwise advertise whichever one it inferred.
- `device_host_enable` (Boolean) Tell devices an explicit address instead of one the controller infers. Set this with `device_host`; on its own it is meaningless.
- `device_web_control_http` (Boolean) Allow reaching an adopted device's own web UI over plain HTTP.

~> That UI takes a password over an unencrypted connection.
- `device_web_control_https` (Boolean) Allow reaching an adopted device's own web UI over HTTPS.
- `firmware_notification` (Boolean) Notify when a controller firmware update is available.
- `host_name` (String) The address the controller believes it is reachable at, used for its own links and portal URLs. See also `device_host`.
- `log_level_type` (String) Logging level mode, e.g. `AUTO`. The per-category levels are read and preserved but not individually settable here.
- `manage_http_port` (Number) Management HTTP port. Changing it moves the UI.
- `manage_https_port` (Number) Management HTTPS port. Changing it moves the UI, and adopted devices reconnect on the new one.
- `name` (String) Controller name, shown in the UI and in its notifications.
- `ntp_enable` (Boolean) Whether the controller uses its own NTP servers rather than the host clock.
- `ntp_servers` (List of String) NTP servers, used when `ntp_enable` is set.
- `portal_http_port` (Number) Captive-portal HTTP port.
- `portal_https_port` (Number) Captive-portal HTTPS port.
- `portal_https_redirect` (Boolean) Redirect portal HTTP to HTTPS.
- `region` (String) Regulatory region, e.g. `United States`.

~> This constrains the channels and transmit power the radios may legally use. Setting it to somewhere you are not is not a way to get more power.
- `time_zone` (String) IANA time zone, e.g. `America/Los_Angeles`. Drives log timestamps and anything scheduled.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The controller's omadac id.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Controller settings are a singleton for the whole controller, so there is
# nothing to address and the import id is ignored. Any string works.
terraform import omada_controller_settings.this controller
```
